verification_level: FAST plus BATCH plus the affected Phase 3 courts; no memory-safety defect found; one trace compatibility repair and one SEED secret-residue repair; focused runtime tests, full library suite serially and with four threads, clippy and fmt. Miri, Loom and ASan NOT_RUN.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the timestamp counter, the sparse-array owner, the native thread object and its state machine, the per-context thread-local family, the civil-time exports, the no-trace profile exports, the uid/service predicates and the SEED block cipher. All eight entries were the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt; none was deferred or skipped. sparse_array.rs and threads_common.rs are shared concurrency mechanisms and were audited without modification.

defects.class: authority-faithful over-clamp of a safe arm
defects.description: OSSL_trace_string computed `len = size.min(80)` for every size above OSSL_TRACE_STRING_MAX, so `full != 0 && text != 0` printed only 80 bytes. The authority's stack fault is confined to `text == 0`, whose masked copy is written into its 81-byte local; with `text != 0` it prints the whole caller buffer safely (`trace.c:544-560`). The clamp now applies only to `text == 0`, and a unit test pins both arms.
defects.divergence: For `full != 0`, `text != 0`, `size > 80` the candidate now returns and prints the full `size`, matching the authority. The recorded safety divergence for `text == 0` is unchanged.

defects.description: SEED_set_key's `x` holds the raw key words and SEED_encrypt/SEED_decrypt's `x` and `out` hold the caller's block and the last round output. The authority leaves all three on the stack. Each is now OPENSSL_cleanse'd on the function's single return path; the EVP cipher context already cleanses the caller-owned key schedule in cipher_data (`src/evp/cipher_ctx.rs:400`).
defects.divergence: No observable behaviour changes; this is a deliberate improvement over the authority's stack residue.

deferred: ASan: no UB repair and no new extent; no sanitizer build (BOUNDARY).
Miri: unavailable on the pinned 1.98.1 toolchain; the thread_arch state machine and threads_common destructor are the best candidates (BOUNDARY).
Loom/TSan: thread_arch.rs and threads_common.rs were audited but not modified; no model-checking run for their ordering protocol (BOUNDARY).
Dependency-graph regeneration: no shared mechanism's contract or semantics was edited; sparse_array.rs and threads_common.rs are unchanged.
Phase 2/4-25 courts: not rebuilt; only trace.rs changed and Phase 3 covers it.
FRF and SEAL; constant-time review (SEED's change is storage cleansing, not a constant-time claim).
not_discharged: All eight files are audited, not SAFETY_DISCHARGED.
The two repairs are a low-severity compatibility correction and a secrecy improvement; neither is a memory-safety repair.
sparse_array.rs and threads_common.rs are shared concurrency mechanisms and were not modified: their source identity and existing evidence are preserved.
thread_arch's join/clean protocol was checked line by line against the 3.6.4 authority but no Loom/TSan evidence was produced.
retained_obligations: sparse_array's values are caller-owned and borrowed; ossl_sa_free releases nodes only and ossl_sa_free_leaves requires the caller to own every value.
sparse_array's walks support a callback that clears the slot it was handed; inserting, growing or freeing the array from a callback is outside the contract, as it is in the authority.
thread_arch's CryptoThread must be live and spawned for join/is_self; native_clean requires no waiter on the condition variable.
threads_common's tables release their nodes only; the values are expected to be cleaned by the ossl_init_thread_start/stop handlers.
threads_common's CRYPTO_THREAD_get_local_ex/set_local_ex require ctx NULL, the (void *)1 sentinel or a live OSSL_LIB_CTX.
time's Tm must be a live writable glibc struct tm; OPENSSL_gmtime delegates to gmtime_r and null inputs answer failure rather than faulting, as recorded in the divergence policy.

trace's OSSL_trace_string requires a live BIO and, when size != 0, at least size readable bytes; the text == 0 arm above 80 bytes is clamped because the authority's own arm overflows its 81-byte local.
seed's SEED_* entry points require the documented byte extents; the key schedule remains caller-owned and is not cleansed by SEED_set_key.
uid's OPENSSL_issetugid assumes the admitted Linux/glibc profile, where getauxval(AT_SECURE) is available.
residuals: rdtsc answers 0 on a non-x86_64 target, selecting the caller's global-seed branch; the admitted profile is linux-x86_64 and the arm is a documented divergence.
trace answers 0/NULL from every channel-setting export under no-trace, exactly as the authority's fall-through bodies do; the category tables and OSSL_trace_string remain live.
documentation_corrections: trace.rs's recorded divergence now states that the authority's overflow is confined to the text == 0 arm, and that the text != 0 arm prints the caller's full buffer safely.
seed.rs now records the secret classification of its local word arrays and the EVP layer's ownership/cleansing of the key schedule.
shared_boundary_files: src/runtime/sparse_array.rs: audited, not modified; its node-ownership model and the callback re-entrancy contract are unchanged.
src/runtime/threads_common.rs: audited, not modified; its source identity and retained obligations are unchanged.
unsafe_operations_introduced: src/seed.rs: three OPENSSL_cleanse calls on live stack arrays, each in an existing unsafe block with a SAFETY comment; no new precondition or boundary.
secret_bearing_buffers: seed.rs: SEED_set_key's raw-key word copy and SEED_encrypt/SEED_decrypt's block and round-output arrays are cleansed on the only return path; the SeedKeySchedule is caller-owned and cleansed by the EVP cipher context's cipher_data release.
trace.rs/uid.rs/rdtsc.rs/time.rs: public metadata only; no secret handling claim.
threads_common: stores caller data pointers (RCU reader state) and deliberately does not own or release them; no secret contents.
sparse_array: values are caller-owned pointers; no secret handling claim.

boundary_control.name: runtime::trace::tests::full_text_above_the_limit_is_not_clamped_but_masked_text_is
boundary_control.reason: The repaired trace arm needed a positive control for the full-text path and a control for the retained text == 0 clamp; both are asserted through a memory BIO. SEED's cleansing is not behaviourally observable, so its control is the existing ECB known-answer test plus code review of the single return path.
